title: Server rendering
summary: Render a request-scoped router, serialize its snapshot, then hydrate with the browser route table.

sections.title: Interactive shells with deferred data
sections.body: Preact renderApplication accepts earlyHydration: true. The browser hydrates the shell while optional nested promises remain pending. Each promise settles independently through the document stream; Await updates its Suspense boundary without rerunning the initial loader. The default still hydrates after document completion. This option requires streaming production hosting: Vite development HTML transformation buffers the document. Measure a successful interaction, not just TTFB or DOMContentLoaded.

sections.title: Load on the server
sections.body: Create a router per request. Passing a Request forwards headers and cancellation. Avoid sharing router state or user data between requests.

sections.title: Hydrate
sections.body: deserialize restores Error objects. A successful hydration snapshot avoids a duplicate initial loader request. Client-only routes render their fallback on the server and load in the browser.

sections.title: Production transport
sections.body: The browser proxy uses the configured dataEndpoint, defaulting to /_smolter, with a local route URL parameter. Match that endpoint in Vite and createRequestHandler. Use distinct app-scoped paths when several applications share one origin.

sections.title: Hosting
sections.body: GitHub Pages serves the browser examples and documentation. It cannot run server loaders. Run apps/react-ssr or apps/preact-ssr on a Node server to try request-time rendering and server mutations.

sections.title: Deferred Preact documents
sections.body: renderApplication starts root and route loaders concurrently. Top-level loader promises determine the initial data and HTTP status; nested promises can remain pending. Consume them with Suspense and Await. With earlyHydration enabled, pending references arrive with the shell and deferred successes or failures settle in the browser independently. A request that closes before settlement rejects unfinished values. Root-loader failures retain root-boundary ownership during hydration. Errors after headers are sent cannot change the HTTP status.

sections.title: Externally injected head elements
sections.body: Whole-document hydration expects the server and client layouts to match. Mark externally injected direct children of head with data-smolter-preserve. mountApplication temporarily excludes those nodes from hydration and restores the same nodes afterward; the application must not also render them. This is an explicit integration contract, not automatic tolerance of arbitrary HTML rewriting. Do not use it for application-owned tags, body content, or changes to the hydration payload.
